correctness.rationale: The exact next-generation Perron cancellation gives Wdot=sum p_i(S_i-s_i)f_i. The continuous positive-part correction has rigorously controlled Dini derivative at S_i=s_i. Every noninfected zero-derivative invariant set is forced to be the DFE: any positive infection creates force in a group, pushes its susceptible value below s_i if at equality, and triggers strict Lyapunov decrease. Compactness proves attraction; infection weight and the stable susceptible error equation prove Lyapunov stability. An included exact rational two-group calculation independently replays algebra, not the infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Multiple infected stages alone do not absorb independently changing susceptible coordinates. The 2012 assumptions are violated by admissible vaccinated states with susceptible excess; the 2013 method does not supply the missing sign. The present extra positive-part term creates that sign directly. Generic method similarity does not imply this particular statement.

originality.rationale: The exact vaccinated equality case is explicitly absent from the motivating paper; it proves strict R0<1 with vaccination and R0<=1 only after eliminating vaccination. The present corrected Perron-plus-positive-part argument applies to all independent vaccination rates. A full relevant 2012 multistage comparison has only one susceptible variable and a dominance assumption invalid for independently varying vaccinated susceptible groups. Other close published models differ in their infection structures. Exact source inspections and the one unresolved access risk are documented; searches alone were not treated as proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The precise gap in the multi-group SAIRS vaccination analysis is the critical R0=1 boundary with heterogeneous nonzero ν_i. Closing it yields the exact disease-elimination threshold for every group count and permits initially excessive susceptible fractions; this is substantively different from a routine strict-inequality extension or numerical improvement. The positive-part correction is motivated directly by a sign-indefinite Perron infection functional.
